note: Property names are Notion display names, verbatim from s1.2-s1.8. One workspace = one client.

Set.note: Notion requires exactly one title per data source, and the title is the row's name everywhere it is read: the Sets table, a relation chip, an @-mention. session-runner derives it from the row's own exercise, set index and magnitudes in titles.name_every_set, which runs on every Sets write leaving the log_set seam, so no handler can produce an unnamed row (ticket workout-log-4sc).

Session.note: The session page id the create call returned, as text. Not a relation: Notion holds logs only, so every value is a string, number, date, select or checkbox and no database points at another.

Exercise.note: The exercise NAME, verbatim. Identity is the name: there is no slug, no id and no catalog database. A name the shipped exercises/defaults.json does not carry is written as typed (session-runner rung 4).

confirm_line.note: The audit trail: what the agent said back (rule L10). One line per entry, not per row, so the non-last rows of a multi-row entry carry an empty string by design. It was the title until workout-log-4sc, which is exactly why it cannot be: those rows landed unnamed. `Set` is the title.

e1RM.expression: if(prop("Set type") == "working" and prop("Reps") >= 1 and prop("Reps") <= 10, prop("Load") * 36 / (37 - prop("Reps")), empty())
e1RM.note: Exact Brzycki, the same rational as loads.brzycki_e1rm (docs/unit-and-magnitude-model.md s2). Notion references properties as prop("Name"); bare identifiers do not parse. The guard is the expression's own if(...), because a formula config accepts no other key: null_when was not a Notion concept and mapped to no API field. Guarding at 10 reps also keeps the divisor at 27 or more, so no rep count bounds.py permits can divide by zero. if(cond, a, b) per https://developers.notion.com/reference/property-object#formula and https://www.notion.com/help/formula-syntax; empty() is Notion's empty value per https://www.notion.com/help/common-formula-errors. tools/schema/check_e1rm.py holds this and read_layer.e1rm to one answer.

Sessions.description: One row per session. s1.4, rules L1-L18.

config/athlete.note: `notion_parent_page_id` is the page the athlete shared, asked for by intake because nothing else can supply it (ticket workout-log-mqs). `timezone` is asked too, because `Sessions.Timezone` is frozen at open (rule L3) and before this an install with no session had nowhere to hold one (ticket workout-log-ayf.16). `notion_data_sources` is the JSON `{database name: data source id}` the create calls returned: no read verb answers "which databases exist", so intake persists what the caller handed it and hydrate.py reads it back.

config/preferences.note: `location` and the plate/bar keys are the gym's equipment reality, which was a `Locations` database row until Notion became logs-only. They are the athlete's own settings, not a log, so they belong on a config page. `min_increment_lb`/`min_increment_kg` are what `program-design/scripts/loads.py` floors a resolved load to; absent, it falls back to the smallest pair a normal gym racks.

program/current.note: `body` is the picked library/*.json template verbatim, JSON encoded, so the rotation a later chat reads is the one this program actually has, swaps included. `started_at` scopes the rotation cursor to this program: the sessions that count are the closed ones that also started at or after it was picked. `progression` is the JSON `{exercise name: {field: value}}` that per-exercise progression state lives in now that there is no `Exercises` row to hang it on: only the fields no reader can derive from the logged sets are here. Round trip owned by .claude/skills/program-design/scripts/program_page.py.
